resolved_findings.issue: Step 4 (the fix for v2's F3) now gives an explicit rename instruction, but still doesn't say which mechanism performs the rename and re-save. Steps 1 and 3 both name a concrete command (`python3 scripts/clean.py ...`, `curl ...`); step 4 just says to 'apply the table yourself... rename it... then re-save the file' without saying whether that happens via a shell one-liner (which would need `Bash`, already declared), a text/file-edit tool, or manual reconstruction of the CSV.
resolved_findings.current_text: 4. If the user doesn't want header names sent to the external service (step 3), apply `references/mapping.md`'s table yourself instead: for each header in the cleaned output that matches a listed variant, rename it to the corresponding canonical name, then re-save the file.
resolved_findings.suggested_rewrite: 4. If the user doesn't want header names sent to the external service (step 3), apply `references/mapping.md`'s table yourself: read the cleaned CSV's header row, rename each header that matches a listed variant to its canonical name, and write the file back out in place (e.g. via a short Python/`csv` snippet run through Bash, consistent with step 1's tooling) rather than reconstructing it by hand.
resolved_findings.why_it_matters: Without a named mechanism, two runs of this step could produce different results (a careful full rewrite of the CSV vs. an ad hoc partial edit that corrupts quoting/delimiters) purely because Claude picked a different way to 're-save the file' each time — the same run-to-run inconsistency risk the original F3 finding was raised over, just one level down.
